name: Auer v. Robbins
summary: The Supreme Court held that an agency's interpretation of its own ambiguous regulation is controlling unless plainly erroneous or inconsistent with the regulation, establishing what became known as Auer deference.
significance: Auer established the doctrine of deference to agencies' interpretations of their own regulations, which is doctrinally parallel to Stinson; the erosion of Auer deference is a key part of the argument for reconsidering Stinson.
